source.title: Fast Multi-dimensional Refusal Subspaces via RFM-AGOP

record.tranche_reason: The study directly tests single- versus multi-direction refusal ablation and reports that one direction is insufficient in larger models, refining the single-direction claim.
record.gate_note: The study directly ablates refusal directions and measures harmful-request ASR, harmless-request refusal under steering, and MMLU retention. It also compares single-direction extraction baselines. Table 1 is flattened in the supplied text, so its numbers cannot be assigned reliably to individual model-method cells; ASR rows use the figures' reported qualitative results and the authors' textual descriptions. The paper's discussion of harmfulness being separately represented cites other work and is not a result of this study.
record.test_reason: The study ablates single directions, including the original DIM direction, and multi-direction subspaces in Qwen 3 reasoning models (1.7B–14B) and Qwen 2.5 7B. It measures HarmBench ASR with random-direction controls, and reports that one direction fails in models of 8B and up. These are its own results bearing on V1, V2, V4 and V8. It is not an original source.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors also state that single-direction ablation fails in Qwen3 models of 8B and up whatever the extraction method (DIM, probe, RFM). They conclude that larger models encode refusal in higher-dimensional subspaces, and that RFM-AGOP extracts such subspaces cheaply and ablates better than its alternatives. What the subspace means remains unclear.
record.recipe_differences: The study includes a Difference-in-Means baseline, but its main method extracts a multi-dimensional subspace with RFM-AGOP rather than the original single difference-in-means direction. It uses last-token residual activations, paired multilingual prompts, and layer-wise weight projection; it does not establish the original all-layer-and-position ablation recipe.
record.method_sensitivity: The outcome varies with model size and number of directions ablated. Harmless-request steering differs by eigenvector; the second direction can produce garbage, while the third through fifth have little or no effect. The paper also reports sensitivity of evaluation to judge prompts and hyperparameters.

fits_no_version.finding: After RFM multi-direction weight ablation, Qwen3 8B keeps its MMLU score while Qwen3 14B drops (cause unexplained).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Ablating a multi-direction refusal subspace preserves general capability.

record.peer_reviewed: Mechanistic Interpretability Workshop at the 43rd International Conference on Machine Learning, 2026
record.problems: The authors describe refusal measurement as difficult and LLM-as-a-judge evaluation as insufficiently rigorous and sensitive to system prompts. The dataset is described as temporary and generated/translated with Qwen 3 8B. Table 1 values are flattened in the supplied text and cannot be assigned reliably to model-method cells; several plotted results are not numerically recoverable from the supplied text. The Qwen 3 14B MMLU drop is unexplained, and the authors question whether steering asymmetries reflect implementation errors or an incomplete understanding of the subspace.
record.rows_left_out: Table 1 contains additional method-by-model ASR cells, but the supplied flattened layout does not support reliable assignment of many values to methods and conditions. They are not transcribed as numeric rows. Figure 3 scores for models other than the two explicitly described in the text are figure-only and have no recoverable values or textual outcome descriptions.

untested.parts: Inducing refusal by adding the DIM direction, and capability retention after DIM ablation. Steering and MMLU were run only with RFM directions.
Released abliterated checkpoints or a named abliteration tool.
Affine or cone geometry as such. The study tests only whether added RFM eigenvectors increase ablation ASR.
Non-Qwen reasoning models; changes in the direction during the reasoning trace; the effect of thinking on/off for ablation.

missing.what: DIM single-direction ablation ASR per model: Qwen2.5 7B 0.65, Qwen3 1.7B 0.80, 4B 0.51, 8B 0.07, 14B 0.06. Vanilla baselines are 0.01, 0.20, 0.02, 0.00 and 0.00.
RCO and Clusters baselines at k=1/3/5, e.g. Qwen3 8B RCO 0.23/0.28/0.34 and Clusters 0.02/0.22/0.37.
Qwen2.5 7B non-reasoning RFM ablation: 0.77, 0.75 and 0.96 at k=1/3/5.
Ablating v2..v5 without v1 sharply reduces ablation efficiency, consistent with a dominant direction.

record.verdict_notes: Table 1 can be parsed by counting entries per column (19 at k=1, 14 at k=3, 14 at k=5 match the method/model layout), but the cell assignment is an inference. The authors attribute single-direction failure to size, yet Qwen2.5 7B (non-reasoning) responds to DIM, so size and reasoning training are confounded. Judge scores are min-max over two LLM judges with 84% agreement. The dataset is multilingual and generated by Qwen3-8B.

versions.untested_parts: The study tests single-direction removal with DIM and other extraction baselines, plus steering with RFM eigenvectors, but does not establish the original claim's exact difference-in-means intervention at every layer and position. Capability retention is measured on MMLU, not broadly across other abilities.
Tests weight edits to the evaluated Qwen models, but does not report releasing edited checkpoints or test a specific separately named abliteration procedure.
Does not test attacks suppressing the direction or training against its ablation.
Tests whether multiple directions are needed for the measured behaviours; does not establish a general affine or cone geometry beyond these experiments.
The study does not separately measure harmfulness judgments and refusal decisions.
Uses multilingual prompts but does not test whether an extracted direction transfers across languages, model variants, or base and instruct models.
Does not vary safety-training method or timing.
Tests Qwen 3 reasoning models, but not other reasoning-model families or the evolution of the direction during the reasoning trace.

The ± spread is unexplained (possibly judge min-max). ASR counts harmful compliance (judge score 3-4), not refusal absence. Models run 4-bit NF4. MMLU covers RFM edits only, figure-only. Qwen3 1.7B random ablation raises ASR 0.22→0.45, so 1.7B multi-direction gains are uncontrolled. The Clusters baseline (per-cluster DIM) gives 14B 0/0.09/0.12 and 8B 0.02/0.22/0.37; it has no rows.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Qwen 3 1.7B and Qwen 3 4B; one-direction ablation and the first RFM direction on harmless prompts
reader_labels.reason: The authors report effective refusal suppression with one direction in smaller models (r1–r2), and the first RFM direction induces harmless-request refusal (r8).

reader_labels.label: challenges
reader_labels.condition: Qwen 3 models at 8B and 14B; one-direction ablation
reader_labels.reason: One direction is insufficient in models of at least 8B; Qwen 3 8B needs at least three directions to exceed 50% ASR (r3–r5).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Qwen 3 8B; steering with the second through fifth RFM directions
reader_labels.reason: The second direction induces refusal only on some sentences and degrades output, while the third through fifth do not meaningfully induce refusal (r9–r12).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.reason: The authors report that one-direction weight ablation effectively suppresses refusal in smaller models (r1–r2).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Qwen 3 8B and 14B weight edits, and MMLU retention
reader_labels.reason: One-direction edits are insufficient in larger models, multiple directions are needed in Qwen 3 8B, and Qwen 3 14B shows an MMLU drop (r3–r7).

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.reason: The reported increase in ASR with subspace dimension and the need for at least three directions to exceed 50% ASR support a multi-direction account in this setting (r3, r5).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.reason: Ablation benefits from multiple directions, but steering effects are asymmetric: the first direction induces refusal, the second is limited and damages output, and later directions do not meaningfully induce refusal (r8–r12).
